text:
Pittsburgh did almost everything it needed to in Dallas except score. The Penguins out-attempted the Stars 65 to 50, put 33 shots on goal to 23, and earned 3.20 expected goals to 2.98 (the quality of their chances). Our replays of every shot gave them a 63% chance to win. Jake Oettinger gave them zero goals.

The only one that counted came at 12:44 of the second. Wyatt Johnston and Mikko Rantanen worked it in, and Joel Kiviranta, a never-drafted forward who came to the NHL out of Finland's Liiga, tipped it past Arturs Silovs on a 10% chance. That goal moved the Stars from 52% to 73% to win, and the Penguins spent the rest of the night pushing against a wall.

The third period was theirs: 1.65 expected goals to 1.30. Justin Brazeau had the best look of the night, a 31% chance in the third, and missed the net. Oettinger's biggest save, by our win-probability numbers, also came on Brazeau in the third. He finished with 33 saves and 3.20 goals saved above expected, a full 0.81 wins added on his own. It was his fifth shutout of the season, which the Toronto Star called league-best. Silovs was good too, 22 saves and 1.46 goals better than expected, and deserved more than a loss.

The Stars have now won five straight, a week after Jamie Benn reached 1,000 career points and a few days after Miro Heiskanen's overtime winner in his return against Vegas. This was a goalie's win: a 1-0 game where Oettinger outplayed the shot chart.

For Pittsburgh, it is four losses in a row (0-4-0), and the noise around the team is getting louder. The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's first-quarter report card handed "Low marks for Sidney Crosby and Erik Karlsson amid a terrible start," and the trade talk around Karlsson, Rickard Rakell and Evgeni Malkin is constant. A night like this, outplaying a hot team and getting nothing, will not quiet any of it. The Penguins beat Dallas in a shootout back on Oct. 10; this time the shootout never came.
headline: Oettinger stops 33 as Stars win fifth straight
